steps.tx: A metabolic crystalline arthropathy resulting from tissue supersaturation and deposition of monosodium urate monohydrate crystals in articular structures defines **gout**. Sustained hyperuricaemia exceeding the physiological saturation threshold of 6.8 milligrams per decilitre leads to crystal precipitation in synovial fluid and avascular tissues. Crystal phagocytosis by resident macrophages triggers assembly of the NLRP3 inflammasome, activating caspase-1 and releasing active interleukin-1-beta. This initiates an explosive neutrophilic inflammatory cascade, producing exquisite articular pain, erythema, swelling, and warmth that characteristically peaks within twenty-four hours.
steps.say: A metabolic crystalline arthropathy resulting from tissue supersaturation and deposition of monosodium urate crystals in articular structures defines gout. Sustained hyperuricaemia exceeding saturation thresholds leads to crystal precipitation in synovial fluid. Crystal phagocytosis by macrophages triggers assembly of the NLRP3 inflammasome, releasing interleukin-1-beta. This initiates an explosive neutrophilic inflammatory response, producing severe articular pain, swelling, and erythema that peaks within twenty-four hours.

steps.tx: Acute crystalline monoarthritis striking the first metatarsophalangeal joint represents the classic initial clinical presentation of acute gout. Termed **podagra**, sudden excruciating pain, marked erythema, and tense cutaneous oedema in the first toe typically erupts in the early morning hours, often provoked by alcohol debauch, red meat ingestion, trauma, or loop diuretic therapy. Over eighty-five percent of initial gout attacks involve the lower extremities, with other common sites including the midfoot, ankle, and knee. Left untreated, acute attacks resolve spontaneously over seven to fourteen days.
steps.say: Acute crystalline monoarthritis striking the first metatarsophalangeal joint represents the classic initial clinical presentation of acute gout. Termed podagra, sudden excruciating pain and erythema in the big toe typically erupts in the early morning hours, often provoked by alcohol, dietary purines, or diuretics. Over eighty percent of initial attacks involve lower extremity joints. Left untreated, acute attacks resolve spontaneously over one to two weeks.

left.title: Acute Gout (Podagra)
points: First MTP joint involved in > 50% of first attacks
Excruciating pain peaking within 12-24 hours
Cutaneous erythema and warmth mimicking cellulitis
Triggers: Alcohol, red meat, trauma, dehydration, diuretics
Serum uric acid can be falsely normal during acute flare

right.title: Acute Septic Arthritis
points: Large joints predominantly (Knee > Hip > Shoulder)
High fever, rigors, and constitutional toxicity
Synovial fluid: Purulent, WBC > 50,000/mcL (> 90% neutrophils)
Gram stain positive and positive bacterial culture
Medical emergency requiring urgent surgical washout

steps.tx: Polarized light microscopy of aspirated synovial fluid provides the definitive gold-standard confirmation of crystal arthropathy. Identifying needle-shaped **monosodium urate crystals** within polymorphonuclear leukocytes demonstrates intense strongly negative birefringence under compensated polarized light. When aligned parallel to the slow axis of the red compensator filter, urate crystals appear bright yellow; when aligned perpendicular to the axis, they turn bright blue. Intracellular phagocytosed crystals establish the definitive diagnosis of acute gouty arthritis, safely differentiating crystalline flares from acute bacterial septic arthritis.
steps.say: Polarized light microscopy of aspirated synovial fluid provides the definitive gold-standard confirmation of crystal arthropathy. Identifying needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals within leukocytes demonstrates intense strongly negative birefringence under compensated polarized light. When aligned parallel to the compensator axis, crystals appear yellow; when perpendicular, they turn blue. Demonstrating intracellular crystals confirms acute gout and distinguishes it from septic arthritis.

vis.caption: Polarized light microscopy displaying needle-shaped negative birefringent monosodium urate crystals in gout. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Chronic unmanaged hyperuricaemia produces destructive nodular granulomatous deposits of monosodium urate crystals in articular and periarticular soft tissues. Developing chronic **tophaceous gout** manifests as firm, chalky, painless nodular deposits termed tophi, characteristically located on the helix of the ear, olecranon bursa, prepatellar bursa, and Achilles tendon. Histopathologically, tophi consist of crystalline urate cores encircled by chronic mononuclear foreign-body granulomas and multinucleated giant cells. Radiographs reveal pathognomonic periarticular punched-out bony erosions with sclerotic margins and overhanging edges (Martel sign), which spare the joint space until late.
steps.say: Chronic unmanaged hyperuricaemia produces destructive nodular granulomatous deposits of monosodium urate crystals in periarticular tissues. Developing chronic tophaceous gout manifests as firm chalky nodules termed tophi, localized on the ear helix, olecranon, and tendons. Histopathology reveals crystalline cores surrounded by foreign-body giant cells. Radiographs reveal pathognomonic punched-out bony erosions with overhanging edges that spare the joint space until late stages.

left.title: Gout Tophi (Monosodium Urate)
points: Ear helix, olecranon bursa, Achilles tendon
Chalky white, firm, gritty subcutaneous nodules
Histology: Foreign-body giant cell granulomas around urate
X-ray: Punched-out erosions with overhanging edges (Martel sign)
Resolves gradually with sustained urate-lowering therapy

right.title: Rheumatoid Nodules (Fibrinoid)
points: Olecranon extensor surfaces, pressure points
Firm, non-tender, rubbery subcutaneous nodules
Histology: Central fibrinoid necrosis, palisading histiocytes
X-ray: Symmetrical marginal joint erosions with osteopenia
Associated with high-titre RF and aggressive RA

steps.tx: First-line pharmacological management of acute gout flares suppresses neutrophil migration and inflammasome activation without altering serum uric acid concentrations. Administering oral **colchicine** binds unpolymerized tubulin dimers, inhibiting microtubule assembly, preventing neutrophil chemotaxis, and blocking NLRP3 inflammasome activation. The recommended dosing schedule is 1.2 milligrams at onset, followed by 0.6 milligrams one hour later. Oral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (naproxen, indomethacin) or oral corticosteroids (prednisolone) provide equivalent anti-inflammatory efficacy in patients with renal impairment where colchicine and NSAIDs are contraindicated.
steps.say: First-line pharmacological management of acute gout flares suppresses neutrophil migration and inflammasome activation without altering serum uric acid concentrations. Administering oral colchicine binds tubulin dimers, inhibiting microtubule assembly, preventing neutrophil chemotaxis, and blocking NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Oral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or systemic corticosteroids provide equivalent anti-inflammatory efficacy in patients with renal impairment.

nodes.label: Colchicine: 1.2 mg immediately, followed by 0.6 mg 1 hour later
Or Full-Dose NSAIDs (Naproxen 500 mg BID / Indomethacin)
If Renal / Cardiac Impairment: Oral Prednisolone (30-40 mg/day)

steps.tx: Long-term prevention of recurrent gout flares and dissolution of tophi requires sustained pharmacological reduction of serum uric acid levels. Administering the purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor **allopurinol** competitively blocks xanthine oxidase, suppressing uric acid synthesis. The clinical target is to maintain serum uric acid strictly below 6.0 milligrams per decilitre (or below 5.0 mg/dL in tophaceous disease). Febuxostat represents a potent non-purine inhibitor for allopurinol-intolerant patients. Prophylactic colchicine or low-dose NSAIDs must be co-prescribed for three to six months to prevent mobilization flares.

Converts insoluble urate to soluble allantoin

steps.tx: An acute crystalline arthropathy mediated by precipitation of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals mimics acute gouty attacks. Termed **pseudogout** (acute calcium pyrophosphate crystal arthritis), the knee is the overwhelmingly most common joint involved (affecting over fifty percent of cases), followed by the wrist and shoulder. Polarized light microscopy of aspirated synovial fluid demonstrates rhomboid or rod-shaped crystals exhibiting weak positive birefringence (appearing blue when aligned parallel to the red compensator axis). Conventional plain radiography reveals pathognomonic chondrocalcinosis, visible as punctate linear radiodensities within articular hyaline cartilage and fibrocartilaginous menisci.

Termed pseudogout, the knee is the overwhelmingly most common joint involved, followed by the wrist. Polarized light microscopy of synovial fluid demonstrates rhomboid crystals exhibiting weak positive birefringence. Conventional radiography reveals pathognomonic chondrocalcinosis, visible as punctate linear radiodensities within articular cartilage and menisci.

left.title: Gout (Monosodium Urate)
points: Needle-shaped intracellular crystals
Strong negative birefringence (Yellow parallel, Blue perpendicular)
Predominantly first MTP joint (Podagra)
Radiology: Punched-out erosions with overhanging edges
Underlying etiology: Hyperuricaemia

right.title: Pseudogout (Calcium Pyrophosphate)
points: Rhomboid or rod-shaped crystals
Weak positive birefringence (Blue parallel, Yellow perpendicular)
Predominantly large joints (Knee > Wrist)
Radiology: Linear chondrocalcinosis in cartilage/menisci
Associated with Haemochromatosis and Hyperparathyroidism

steps.tx: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease strongly associates with specific underlying metabolic and endocrine disorders in young patients presenting before age sixty. Young individuals presenting with chondrocalcinosis mandate screening for hereditary haemochromatosis (measuring ferritin and transferrin saturation), primary hyperparathyroidism (measuring calcium and parathyroid hormone), and hypomagnesaemia. Furthermore, an X-linked recessive inborn error of purine metabolism causes profound hyperuricaemia in young males. In **lesch-nyhan syndrome**, complete deficiency of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HPRT) leads to massive purine overproduction, presenting with severe juvenile gout, choreoathetosis, cognitive impairment, and compulsive self-mutilation.
steps.say: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease strongly associates with specific underlying metabolic disorders in young patients presenting before age sixty. Furthermore, an inborn error of purine metabolism causes severe hyperuricaemia in young males. In lesch-nyhan syndrome, HPRT deficiency produces juvenile gout, choreoathetosis, and compulsive self-mutilation.
